## Introduction

The Sim et al. donors span foetal, young and adult hearts, but each
donor gives only one age label. Within one age group, cardiomyocytes can
still differ in how mature they are. Module 2 gives each cardiomyocyte a
single number for its position along maturation: **pseudotime**.

Pseudotime orders cells so that cells close together in a biological
process get close values. It is not real time, and its scale is
arbitrary: only the *ordering* matters. Which end counts as "early" is a
separate choice, and for many methods it has to be supplied.

### Two ways to order cardiomyocytes

We use a standard workflow: a PCA of gene expression, then two
trajectory methods on that PCA.

1. **Slingshot,** a *principal-curve* method. It clusters cells, links
   the cluster centres into a tree, fits a smooth curve through it, and
   projects every cell onto the curve. Pseudotime is the distance along
   the curve.
2. **Diffusion pseudotime (DPT)** with the destiny package. It builds a
   graph of similar cells and measures how far a random walk travels
   from a root cell.

Both methods need to be told where maturation starts. We use one number
from Module 1 for that: each cell's Φ-Space `fetal` score. We then check
the two pseudotimes against each other and against the donors' ages,
which neither method sees.

Two optional sections follow the handoff to Module 3. **Extension A**
shows a common pitfall: slingshot's answer depends on how you cluster
the cells. **Extension B** repeats the analysis on the Φ-Space scores
from Module 1 instead of PCA, and adds a pseudotime computed from the
Φ-Space scores alone.


## Load Libraries and Module 1 Output

```{r load-libraries}
library(SingleCellExperiment)
library(slingshot)
library(destiny)
library(scater)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tibble)
library(patchwork)
library(RColorBrewer)
```

Module 1 handed over a single file: the query with Φ-Space scores in
`reducedDim`, scran logcounts in `assay(query, "logcounts")`, and the
per-cell annotations (`PhiCellType`, `PhiCellTypeBroad`, `PhiAge`,
`group`, …) in `colData`.

```{r load-module1}
query <- readRDS(file.path(results_dir, "05_phispace_query.rds"))

cat("Assays:      ", paste(assayNames(query), collapse = ", "), "\n")
cat("reducedDims: ", paste(reducedDimNames(query), collapse = ", "), "\n")
cat("Cells:       ", ncol(query), "\n")
cat("Broad types: ", paste(sort(unique(query$PhiCellTypeBroad)),
                            collapse = ", "), "\n")
```

```{r cache-setup}
results_dir <- Sys.getenv("SCW_RESULTS", "../results")
dir.create(results_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
```

## Subset to Cardiomyocytes

Cardiomyocytes carry the foetal→adult maturation signal we want to
trace. Running pseudotime on all cell types at once would mix several
biological processes into one trajectory. We select them with the broad
cell-type labels from Module 1.

```{r subset-cm}
cm <- query[, query$PhiCellTypeBroad == "Cardiomyocyte"]
cat("Cardiomyocytes:", ncol(cm), "\n")
print(table(cm$group))
```

## PCA, and a UMAP for Plotting

Both trajectory methods work on a **PCA** of gene expression: we select
highly variable genes and keep the first 20 principal components.

```{r pca-expression}
pca_cache <- file.path(results_dir, "06_cm_pca.rds")

if (file.exists(pca_cache)) {
    cm <- readRDS(pca_cache)
    message("Loaded cached CM object with PCA from ", pca_cache)
} else {
    # Highly variable gene selection
    gene_var <- rowVars(as.matrix(logcounts(cm)))
    names(gene_var) <- rownames(cm)
    n_hvg <- min(2000, nrow(cm))
    hvg <- names(sort(gene_var, decreasing = TRUE))[seq_len(n_hvg)]

    pca <- prcomp(t(as.matrix(logcounts(cm)[hvg, ])),
                  center = TRUE, scale. = FALSE)
    reducedDim(cm, "PCA") <- pca$x[, 1:20]
    saveRDS(cm, pca_cache)
}

cat("PCA dims:", paste(dim(reducedDim(cm, "PCA")), collapse = " x "), "\n")
```

To display pseudotimes we also need a 2D map of the cells. We compute a
UMAP from the PCA. Neither pseudotime method uses the UMAP; it is only
for plotting, so that every result is drawn on the same layout.

`n_neighbors = 15` and `min_dist = 0.5` were chosen by trying several
settings: smaller `n_neighbors` broke the cardiomyocyte continuum into
islands with no biological meaning.

```{r umap}
umap_cache <- file.path(results_dir, "06_cm_umap.rds")

if (file.exists(umap_cache)) {
    reducedDim(cm, "UMAP") <- readRDS(umap_cache)
    message("Loaded cached UMAP")
} else {
    set.seed(42)
    cm <- scater::runUMAP(cm, dimred = "PCA", name = "UMAP",
                          n_neighbors = 15, min_dist = 0.5)
    saveRDS(reducedDim(cm, "UMAP"), umap_cache)
}
```

A few small helpers for the plots and runs below:

```{r helpers}
umap_df <- as.data.frame(reducedDim(cm, "UMAP"))
colnames(umap_df) <- c("UMAP1", "UMAP2")

# Rescale to [0, 1] so different methods share one colour scale
rescale01 <- function(x) {
    x <- x - min(x, na.rm = TRUE)
    x / max(x, na.rm = TRUE)
}

# UMAP coloured by a pseudotime (blue = early, red = late)
umap_base <- function(pt_vec) {
    ggplot(cbind(umap_df, pt = pt_vec), aes(UMAP1, UMAP2, colour = pt)) +
        geom_point(size = 0.4, alpha = 0.7) +
        scale_colour_distiller(palette = "Spectral", name = "Pseudotime") +
        theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
        theme(aspect.ratio = 1)
}

# Slingshot curves, re-fitted in UMAP space for display
embed_curves_df <- function(sds, label) {
    curves <- slingCurves(embedCurves(sds, reducedDim(cm, "UMAP")))
    do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(curves), function(i) {
        s <- curves[[i]]$s[curves[[i]]$ord, , drop = FALSE]
        data.frame(UMAP1 = s[, 1], UMAP2 = s[, 2],
                   lineage = paste0(label, "_L", i))
    }))
}
with_curves <- function(p, crv_df) {
    p + geom_path(data = crv_df, aes(UMAP1, UMAP2, group = lineage),
                  inherit.aes = FALSE, colour = "grey30", linewidth = 0.8)
}

# Run slingshot, or load a cached run
run_slingshot <- function(cache, dimred, clusters, start) {
    fp <- file.path(results_dir, cache)
    if (file.exists(fp)) {
        message("Loaded cached ", cache)
        return(readRDS(fp))
    }
    sds <- slingshot(
        reducedDim(cm, dimred),
        clusterLabels = clusters,
        start.clus    = start,
        dist.method   = "simple"
    )
    saveRDS(sds, fp)
    sds
}

# One pseudotime per cell: the mean over slingshot's lineages
lineage_pt <- function(sds) rowMeans(slingPseudotime(sds), na.rm = TRUE)
```

`dist.method = "simple"` is needed because slingshot's default distance
fails when some clusters are very small.

## Cluster the Cardiomyocytes

Slingshot builds its tree on clusters, so we first cluster the cells.
We use the standard graph-based approach: a shared-nearest-neighbour
(SNN) graph on the PCA, split into communities with the Louvain
algorithm.

```{r clusters, fig.width=7, fig.height=5.5}
cluster_cache <- file.path(results_dir, "06_cm_clusters.rds")
if (file.exists(cluster_cache)) {
    cm$cluster <- readRDS(cluster_cache)
    message("Loaded cached clusters")
} else {
    set.seed(42)
    snn <- scran::buildSNNGraph(cm, use.dimred = "PCA", k = 20)
    cm$cluster <- factor(igraph::cluster_louvain(snn)$membership)
    saveRDS(cm$cluster, cluster_cache)
}
print(table(cm$cluster))

clust_levels <- levels(cm$cluster)
clust_pal <- c(brewer.pal(9, "Set1"), brewer.pal(8, "Dark2"),
               brewer.pal(8, "Set2"))[seq_along(clust_levels)]
names(clust_pal) <- clust_levels

ggplot(cbind(umap_df, cluster = cm$cluster),
       aes(UMAP1, UMAP2, colour = cluster)) +
    geom_point(size = 0.4, alpha = 0.7) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = clust_pal) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
    theme(aspect.ratio = 1) +
    guides(colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 2))) +
    labs(title = "Louvain clusters (SNN graph on PCA)")
```

## Where Does Maturation Start?

Both methods need a starting point: slingshot a **starting cluster**,
DPT a **root cell**. We could pick it by eye from marker genes. Here we
use Module 1's Φ-Space `fetal` score, which says how much each cell
looks like foetal reference cells.

```{r fetal-score, fig.width=13, fig.height=5.5}
cm$fetal_score <- reducedDim(cm, "PhiSpace")[, "fetal"]

p_group <- ggplot(cbind(umap_df, group = cm$group),
                  aes(UMAP1, UMAP2, colour = group)) +
    geom_point(size = 0.4, alpha = 0.7) +
    scale_colour_brewer(palette = "Set1") +
    theme_bw(base_size = 11) + theme(aspect.ratio = 1) +
    guides(colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 3))) +
    labs(title = "Donor stage", colour = "Stage")

p_fetal <- ggplot(cbind(umap_df, fetal = cm$fetal_score),
                  aes(UMAP1, UMAP2, colour = fetal)) +
    geom_point(size = 0.4, alpha = 0.7) +
    scale_colour_gradient(low = "white", high = "blue") +
    theme_bw(base_size = 11) + theme(aspect.ratio = 1) +
    labs(title = "Φ-Space fetal score", colour = "fetal")

p_group | p_fetal
```

The starting cluster is the cluster with the highest mean `fetal` score.
The root cell is the cell with the highest `fetal` score.

```{r pick-start}
mean_fetal_by <- function(cluster_vec) {
    tibble(cluster = cluster_vec, fetal = cm$fetal_score) |>
        group_by(cluster) |>
        summarise(mean_fetal = mean(fetal), n = n(), .groups = "drop") |>
        arrange(desc(mean_fetal))
}

anchor_tbl <- mean_fetal_by(cm$cluster)
anchor_tbl
start_cluster <- as.character(anchor_tbl$cluster[1])
root_cell     <- which.max(cm$fetal_score)
cat("start.clus:", start_cluster, "\n")
cat("Root cell index:", root_cell,
    " (fetal score =", round(cm$fetal_score[root_cell], 3), ")\n")
```

## Pseudotime 1: Slingshot

```{r slingshot}
sling <- run_slingshot("06_slingshot_pca_unsup.rds",
                       "PCA", cm$cluster, start_cluster)
cm$pt_slingshot <- lineage_pt(sling)
cat("Lineages found:", length(slingLineages(sling)), "\n")
slingLineages(sling)
```

Each lineage is a path through the cluster tree, from the starting
cluster to one end point. `slingPseudotime()` returns one column per
lineage; we average them to get one pseudotime per cell.

```{r slingshot-umap, fig.width=7, fig.height=6}
curves_df <- embed_curves_df(sling, "sling")
with_curves(umap_base(rescale01(cm$pt_slingshot)), curves_df) +
    labs(title = "Slingshot pseudotime, with its principal curves")
```

All seven lineages start in cluster 7. Four run through clusters 3 and
4 to the clusters on the right of the UMAP, where the post-natal nuclei
are. The other three are short branches into neighbouring clusters. The
curves are fitted in PCA space and only re-fitted in UMAP space for
display, so they can look tangled on the UMAP.

## Pseudotime 2: Diffusion Pseudotime (DPT)

```{r destiny-dpt}
dpt_cache <- file.path(results_dir, "06_dpt_pca.rds")

if (file.exists(dpt_cache)) {
    dpt <- readRDS(dpt_cache)
    message("Loaded cached DPT result")
} else {
    dm  <- DiffusionMap(as.matrix(reducedDim(cm, "PCA")),
                        n_eigs = 20, sigma = "local", verbose = FALSE)
    dpt <- DPT(dm, tips = root_cell)
    saveRDS(dpt, dpt_cache)
}

cm$pt_dpt <- dpt$dpt
summary(cm$pt_dpt)
```

Without `tips`, destiny would pick end points itself. We set the root
explicitly so that DPT starts from the same place as slingshot.

## Do the Two Pseudotimes Agree?

With real data there is no ground-truth ordering to check against, and
no single pseudotime method is best for every dataset. In practice you
run a few methods and ask which orderings make sense. This section shows
three simple checks that work for any set of pseudotimes:

- **look** at them on the same map: do they put the same cells early
  and late?
- **correlate** them with each other: do they agree on the order?
- **compare** them with information none of them used, here the donors'
  stage: does the order match what we know about the biology?

### On the UMAP

```{r compare-umap, fig.width=12, fig.height=5.5}
cm$pt_slingshot_01 <- rescale01(cm$pt_slingshot)
cm$pt_dpt_01       <- rescale01(cm$pt_dpt)

# `+` binds tighter than `|`, so wrap the whole layout before adding
# plot_layout(); otherwise it applies to the last panel only.
((with_curves(umap_base(cm$pt_slingshot_01), curves_df) +
      labs(title = "Slingshot")) |
    (umap_base(cm$pt_dpt_01) + labs(title = "DPT"))) +
    plot_layout(guides = "collect")
```

### By rank correlation

Each method has its own scale, and only the *order* of cells matters, so
we compare them with Spearman (rank) correlation.

```{r compare-cor}
pt_mat <- data.frame(
    Slingshot = cm$pt_slingshot,
    DPT       = cm$pt_dpt
)
round(cor(pt_mat, use = "complete.obs", method = "spearman"), 3)
```

The two pseudotimes agree closely on the order of cells (ρ = 0.85),
although one fits curves through clusters and the other uses no
clusters at all.

### Against donor stage

The donors' stage is **held-out information**: no method saw it. If a
pseudotime captures maturation, its values should rise from foetal to
young to adult donors.

```{r compare-stage, fig.width=8, fig.height=4}
stage_df <- pt_mat |>
    mutate(group = factor(cm$group, levels = c("fetal", "young", "adult"))) |>
    tidyr::pivot_longer(-group, names_to = "method", values_to = "pseudotime") |>
    group_by(method) |>
    mutate(pseudotime = rescale01(pseudotime),
           method = factor(method, levels = colnames(pt_mat)))

ggplot(stage_df, aes(group, pseudotime, fill = group)) +
    geom_violin(scale = "width", alpha = 0.8) +
    geom_boxplot(width = 0.15, alpha = 0.6, outlier.size = 0.3) +
    scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set1") +
    facet_wrap(~ method, nrow = 1) +
    labs(x = "Donor stage", y = "Pseudotime (rescaled)",
         title = "Do the pseudotimes recover the foetal → adult order?") +
    theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
    theme(legend.position = "none")
```

What the plot shows:

- **Both put foetal nuclei clearly first.** The biggest change in this
  data is between the foetal and the post-natal heart.
- **Neither separates young from adult donors well.** With slingshot,
  adult nuclei sit only slightly later than young ones, and the two
  distributions overlap. Within the post-natal heart, maturity varies
  about as much within an age group as between them.
- **DPT is nearly all-or-nothing:** foetal nuclei sit near 0 and almost
  all post-natal nuclei near 0.9. It orders the foetal-to-post-natal
  transition but says little about differences after birth.
- **Some foetal nuclei get a mid-range pseudotime.** Most of them are in
  cluster 8, the separate island of foetal nuclei at the bottom of the
  UMAP. Pseudotime measures distance from the root, so a distinct
  foetal subtype at the end of a branch can look "late".

The spread *within* each stage shows how much nuclei from donors of the
same age differ, which is exactly what a single age label hides.

## Handing Off to Module 3

We save the cardiomyocytes, with their UMAP and pseudotimes, for
Module 3.

```{r save-for-module3}
final_cache <- file.path(results_dir, "06_cm_pseudotime.rds")
saveRDS(cm, final_cache)
cat("Annotated CM object at", final_cache, "\n")
```

In addition to everything Module 1 handed over, the object carries:

- `reducedDim(cm, "PCA")` and `reducedDim(cm, "UMAP")`;
- `cluster`, the Louvain clusters, and `fetal_score`;
- `pt_slingshot` and `pt_dpt`, the two pseudotimes, and their
  `*_01` versions rescaled to `[0, 1]`.

## Summary

- Pseudotime orders cells along a process. It is not real time, and
  most methods need to be told where the process starts.
- We ordered the cardiomyocytes with slingshot (principal curves through
  a cluster tree) and DPT (diffusion from a root cell), both on a PCA of
  gene expression. They agree with each other (ρ = 0.85) and put foetal
  nuclei first; neither separates young from adult donors well.
- With no ground truth, compare several methods with each other and with
  information they did not use.
- (Extension A) The clustering given to slingshot changes the shape of
  the trajectory (how many branches), even when its agreement with donor
  age barely changes.
- (Extension B) Building the trajectories on Module 1's Φ-Space scores
  instead of PCA gives the same agreement with donor age, but a
  different ordering in the details.

## Extension A (Optional): Slingshot Depends on the Clustering

This section is optional: Module 3 does not need it, and we may skip it
in the live session if time is short.

Slingshot builds its tree on **cluster centres**: the clustering you give
it is a modelling choice, not a preprocessing detail.

**Think first.** Above, slingshot used `r if (data_ok) nlevels(cm$cluster) else "the"`
unsupervised Louvain clusters, which know nothing about cell biology.
Suppose we give it the fine Φ-Space cell types from Module 1 instead
(`Cardiomyocyte:Fetal_enriched_metabolic`, `:Metabolic`, `:Stressed`,
…): fewer groups, each defined by a reference atlas.

1. How do you expect the *shape* of the trajectory (the number of
   branches) to change?
2. Do you expect the agreement with donor stage to change as much?

Write down your guesses, then run the code below.

<details>
<summary>What we found</summary>

1. With fewer clusters, slingshot has fewer cluster centres to connect,
   so the tree gets fewer branches (lineages): 3 instead of 7. The
   curves, and therefore what "pseudotime" means for a given cell,
   change visibly.
2. The agreement with donor stage barely changes (ρ = 0.73 instead of
   0.72). A single summary check can look fine even when the
   trajectories themselves differ, which is why it is worth looking at
   the trajectory, not only at one number.

</details>

```{r sensitivity-run}
print(sort(table(cm$PhiCellType), decreasing = TRUE))

start_cluster_phict <- as.character(mean_fetal_by(cm$PhiCellType)$cluster[1])
sling_phict <- run_slingshot("06_slingshot_pca_phict.rds",
                             "PCA", cm$PhiCellType, start_cluster_phict)
cm$pt_sling_phict <- lineage_pt(sling_phict)
```

```{r sensitivity-figure, fig.width=12, fig.height=5.5}
curves_phict_df <- embed_curves_df(sling_phict, "phict")

((with_curves(umap_base(cm$pt_slingshot_01), curves_df) +
      labs(title = "Louvain clusters (main analysis)")) |
    (with_curves(umap_base(rescale01(cm$pt_sling_phict)), curves_phict_df) +
         labs(title = "Φ-Space cell types"))) +
    plot_layout(guides = "collect") +
    plot_annotation(title = "Slingshot on PCA with two clusterings")
```

Two numbers per run make the comparison concrete: how many lineages
(branches) slingshot found, and how well the pseudotime agrees with donor
stage.

```{r sensitivity-table}
stage_num <- as.numeric(factor(cm$group, levels = c("fetal", "young", "adult")))
sling_runs <- list(
    "Louvain clusters"   = sling,
    "Φ-Space cell types" = sling_phict
)
tibble(
    clusters  = names(sling_runs),
    lineages  = vapply(sling_runs, function(s) length(slingLineages(s)), integer(1)),
    spearman_vs_stage = vapply(sling_runs, function(s)
        round(cor(lineage_pt(s), stage_num, method = "spearman"), 2), numeric(1))
)
```

The lesson: **don't trust one trajectory or one check.** Look at the
structure of the trajectory itself, compare it with independent
information such as donor age, and compare it with a method that does not
need a clustering, such as DPT.

## Extension B (Optional): Pseudotime from Φ-Space

This section is not needed for Module 3. It asks whether Module 1's
Φ-Space scores can replace PCA as the space a trajectory is built in.

### The Φ-Space score as a pseudotime

The simplest ordering needs no trajectory model. The reference has four
age groups (`fetal`, `young`, `middle`, `old`). We average the three
post-natal scores into an "adult" score and subtract the `fetal` score:

$$\text{Φ-Space score} = \text{mean}(\text{young}, \text{middle}, \text{old}) - \text{fetal}$$

Module 3 uses this score to pick genes associated with maturation.

The raw difference has long tails, which squash the colour scale, so for
display we also show a cube-root version (`sign(x) · |x|^(1/3)`). It
compresses the tails without changing the order of cells.

```{r phi-score, fig.width=13, fig.height=5.5}
phi_scores  <- reducedDim(cm, "PhiSpace")
adult_score <- rowMeans(phi_scores[, c("young", "middle", "old")])
cm$pt_phi_score    <- adult_score - cm$fetal_score
cm$pt_phi_score_cr <- sign(cm$pt_phi_score) * abs(cm$pt_phi_score)^(1/3)

(umap_base(cm$pt_phi_score) + labs(title = "Φ-Space score (adult − fetal)")) |
    (umap_base(cm$pt_phi_score_cr) +
         labs(title = "Φ-Space score (cube-root, for display)"))
```

### Slingshot and DPT on Φ-Space

We rerun both methods with the Φ-Space scores as the embedding. Everything
else stays the same: the Louvain clusters, the starting cluster and the
root cell. Only the embedding changes.

```{r phi-runs}
sling_phi <- run_slingshot("06_slingshot_phi_unsup.rds",
                           "PhiSpace", cm$cluster, start_cluster)
cm$pt_sling_phi <- lineage_pt(sling_phi)

dpt_phi_cache <- file.path(results_dir, "06_dpt_phispace.rds")
if (file.exists(dpt_phi_cache)) {
    dpt_phi <- readRDS(dpt_phi_cache)
    message("Loaded cached DPT/PhiSpace result")
} else {
    dm_phi <- DiffusionMap(as.matrix(reducedDim(cm, "PhiSpace")),
                           n_eigs = 20, sigma = "local", verbose = FALSE)
    dpt_phi <- DPT(dm_phi, tips = root_cell)
    saveRDS(dpt_phi, dpt_phi_cache)
}
cm$pt_dpt_phi <- dpt_phi$dpt
```

```{r umap-pt-plots, fig.width=12, fig.height=10}
curves_phi_df <- embed_curves_df(sling_phi, "phi")

p_sling_pca <- with_curves(umap_base(cm$pt_slingshot_01), curves_df) +
    labs(title = "slingshot / PCA")
p_sling_phi <- with_curves(umap_base(rescale01(cm$pt_sling_phi)),
                           curves_phi_df) +
    labs(title = "slingshot / Φ-Space")
p_dpt_pca <- umap_base(cm$pt_dpt_01) + labs(title = "DPT / PCA")
p_dpt_phi <- umap_base(rescale01(cm$pt_dpt_phi)) + labs(title = "DPT / Φ-Space")

((p_sling_pca | p_sling_phi) / (p_dpt_pca | p_dpt_phi)) +
    plot_layout(guides = "collect") +
    plot_annotation(title = "Pseudotime on UMAP: two methods × two embeddings")
```

If all four panels show the same blue → red gradient over the same UMAP
regions, the trajectory is robust. If the two slingshot panels agree
with each other but not with the DPT panels, that is a *method* effect;
if the two PCA panels agree but the two Φ-Space panels do not, it is an
*embedding* effect.

### Correlations and agreement with donor stage

```{r pt-cor}
pt_mat5 <- data.frame(
    `slingshot/PCA`      = cm$pt_slingshot,
    `slingshot/PhiSpace` = cm$pt_sling_phi,
    `DPT/PCA`            = cm$pt_dpt,
    `DPT/PhiSpace`       = cm$pt_dpt_phi,
    `Φ-Space score`      = cm$pt_phi_score,
    check.names = FALSE
)
round(cor(pt_mat5, use = "complete.obs", method = "spearman"), 3)
round(sapply(pt_mat5, cor, y = stage_num, method = "spearman"), 2)
```

The second line is each pseudotime's Spearman correlation with donor
stage (foetal = 1, young = 2, adult = 3).

What the numbers show:

- **The embedding changes the order more than the method does.** On
  PCA, slingshot and DPT agree closely (ρ = 0.85). The same method on
  the two embeddings agrees less (ρ = 0.62 for both slingshot and DPT).
- **All five orderings agree with donor stage about equally**
  (ρ = 0.72–0.75). As in Extension A, this one check cannot tell them
  apart.
- **The Φ-Space score agrees well with the main analysis** (ρ = 0.79
  with slingshot and 0.78 with DPT on PCA). Module 3 uses this score
  because it needs no trajectory model, clusters or root cell.

The figure shows one difference that the correlations hide. DPT on
Φ-Space places cluster 8, the separate island of foetal nuclei, at the
start with the other foetal nuclei; DPT on PCA places it midway. A
likely reason is that Φ-Space describes each cell by its similarity to
the reference age groups, so a foetal subtype with a distinct expression
profile still looks foetal.
